applicable_when: The conv2d_bias_relu_kernel iterates K as a flat range [0, TOTAL_K) where TOTAL_K=IN_C*KH*KW, then decodes: in_c=offs_k%IN_C, kw_=(offs_k//IN_C)%KW, kh_=offs_k//(IN_C*KW). Within each BLOCK_K tile, consecutive offs_k values differ only in in_c (fastest-varying), BUT across BLOCK_K boundaries the tile mixes different (kh, kw) positions. When tl.dot stages x_tile (BLOCK_M x BLOCK_K) and w_tile (BLOCK_K x BLOCK_N) through shared memory, the mixed (kh, kw, in_c) indexing within a single BLOCK_K slice creates non-unit strides that cause 7.6-way average bank conflicts (58% excessive wavefronts). The fix is to restructure into three explicit nested loops: for kh in range(KH): for kw in range(KW): for ic_start in range(0, IN_C, BLOCK_K). Each innermost tile then covers a contiguous in_c range at a fixed (kh, kw), giving stride-1 access in both X (NHWC, s_xc=1) and W (OKHWI, s_wi=1), eliminating the bank conflict root cause. The previous attempt (item_id=14c02339) timed out due to an implementation bug, not a fundamental incompatibility.

Its current implementation loads a full BLOCK_SIZE tile of bias values via tl.load(bias_ptr + bias_offsets) and then uses tl.gather(bias_tile, chan_idx % BLOCK_SIZE, 0) to select per-thread bias values. This tl.gather is the root cause of L1TEX stalls: (1) it forces a BLOCK_SIZE-wide bias load even when channels << BLOCK_SIZE, wasting bandwidth; (2) the gather itself is a non-coalesced indirect access that serializes into multiple L1TEX transactions; (3) when BLOCK_SIZE > channels, chan_idx % BLOCK_SIZE wraps incorrectly for tiles spanning channel boundaries. The fix is to restructure to a 2D grid: pid_c = tl.program_id(0) selects one channel, pid_s = tl.program_id(1) selects a spatial tile. Each CTA handles exactly one channel, so bias is a single scalar load (broadcast to all threads in the warp, 1 L2 transaction vs BLOCK_SIZE transactions). The x and out loads remain perfectly coalesced across the spatial dimension. This eliminates the tl.gather entirely and resolves the L1TEX stall bottleneck. The previous attempt (item eb6d97ee) crashed at compile time due to implementation bugs, not a fundamental incompatibility with the approach.
